pass_clause_text: - **Anything else** is recorded as `needs_attention` or failed, with its reason.
frozen_acceptance.next_trial_rule_text: - **When the next trial may start:** only after the previous trial ends `passed` or `completed_no_signals`, or after a `recover` that passed, with no 429 in any of its attempts. The last start is 09:15 ET.
stop_rule_text: a preflight refusal other than benchmark quote age;
six benchmark refusals in a row;
a scan with no fired symbol;
frozen_acceptance.evaluation: A trial is pass only if every clause holds: engine status passed or completed_no_signals; flat; end reconciliation cash_match and positions_match true; 0 open orders; totals.pnl_consistent true; execution_stats.duplicate_executions 0 and no unexplained broker/ledger difference in the broker reconciliation; ledger_risk.halted_reason null at the trial's end; no HTTP 429 in the receipt's HTTP observations, no transport rate_limited mark and no non-200 scan page. A trial with a failed clause is needs_attention when the engine itself reported needs_attention, and fail otherwise; a clause the files cannot evaluate is recorded as null, and a trial whose verdict rests on such a clause would be inconclusive. The verdict ignores what the engine or the driver printed.

forms.sent 1000 (OK); then received 1000 (OK): the closing handshake completed: close code 1000 sent and received; websockets raises ConnectionClosedOK (protocol.py:237-245)
forms.sent 1000 (OK); no close frame received: the client sent close code 1000 and received no close frame; websockets raises ConnectionClosedError, the closing handshake did not complete (exceptions.py:118-131 and 168-175, protocol.py:237-245; the deprecated code attribute then reads 1006, abnormal closure, exceptions.py:142-143)
forms.no close frame received or sent: neither side sent a close frame; websockets raises ConnectionClosedError (same source)

limitations: Metadata plus broker-reconciled evidence, not a frozen gate run. It qualifies no gate.
The broker read uses the same broker API and account as the engine, so it is independent of the engine code but not of the broker.
Alpaca paper fills are simulated by the broker from quotes. They are not exchange executions and do not establish live slippage, queue position or partial-fill behaviour.
Mechanics only: the protocol's development study passed 0 of 768 rule-exits, so no result here evaluates a strategy.
paper_compare.py was not run (decision 11: the tool is not checked against b528bb55 receipts), so no historical fill-model comparison is recorded.

The engine logs carry no timestamps, so websocket and stream-gap lines cannot be placed in time. The 2026-09-23 isolation check's committed output (trials/20260923b-needs-attention/transport-isolation-1e2c96a.json, transport 1e2c96a) recorded a trading-stream line with a completed closing handshake 0.016 s and a data-stream line with no close frame received 0.018 s after the engine's stop() was called, and no restart line before it; its README names only the trading-stream line. These runs neither confirm nor rule out the same timing.

Account designation: the series kept its own engine ledger (the new account-2 root, shared with ext-20260929) but traded broker account alpaca-paper-2, which blueprints/us-equities/incentive-monitor/forward-protocol-v1.json:63 and docs/secret-storage.md:17 designate as the isolated incentive-monitor study account. Whether this use fits the forward study's isolation is referred to the forward protocol's owner, the trading lane; this receipt does not decide it.

The journal holds no exit record for the series unit or the incentive monitor (journal_query). Their results (success, exit status 0) come from the systemd user manager's state, read on 2026-09-30 (units[].manager_state); the manager has run since 2026-09-24, but a manager restart would clear that state. The driver's last line reads series ends: past last start 0915 ET.

Fees: the broker posted REG, TAF and CAT fees for 2026-09-29 on account 2, -0.47 USD in total, for this series and ext-20260929 together; it posts one activity per fee type per day for the account, so its records cannot split them between the two series, and no split is made. The engine has no fee model, so no figure here includes them except the joint fee-inclusive figure (series_totals.joint_pre_and_ext_20260929, -17.90).
evidence_note: Built from the private series workspace (the engine's own receipts, consoles, logs and events), a read-only snapshot of account 2's mover ledger, the systemd user journal, git show b528bb55 and the coordinator's read-only broker reconciliation (GET only, paper endpoint), whose stdout is committed here. Figures present in two or more of those sources were cross-checked by assertion, and a mismatch stops the build; field_provenance names the rest.
